bundles.when_i_would_meet_it: I would not; a recruiter sets up the role before I ever look at the numbers, maybe I hear about it in a weekly catch-up.
bundles.why: Setup is the recruiters' job and I only care that the protected-traits block keeps us legal.

bundles.when_i_would_meet_it: Only indirectly, when a recruiter tells me CVs are processed faster than before.
bundles.why: I assume any hiring tool reads CVs; I do not want to see how it does it.

bundles.when_i_would_meet_it: Monday before the CEO meeting, when I ask what the shortlist for the data role looks like and who the best three are.
bundles.why: This is the closest thing to the answer I need, though I would be annoyed it is filtered not ranked, so I want a clear answer for the CEO.

bundles.when_i_would_meet_it: When a recruiter says someone is interview-ready or a candidate complains about being asked for documents.
bundles.why: Checked claims protect us from bad hires and legal trouble, but it is the recruiters' work, not mine.

bundles.when_i_would_meet_it: When a rejected candidate complains or threatens a claim and I need to know what we told them.
bundles.why: As head of people I worry about discrimination claims, so specific, approved feedback is real protection.

bundles.when_i_would_meet_it: Once a week on my laptop, five minutes before the CEO meeting, to show that hiring got faster.
bundles.why: It is the only screen I use myself and it gives me the time-to-interview-ready number for the CEO; I would want it to show a top three but accept it will not.

proof_timing.why: Asking everyone for documents upfront would put off good candidates and raise data-protection questions, whereas asking only shortlisted people with a stated reason is fair and defensible.
